item.title: GUITION ESP32-S31 development kit features 7-inch capacitive touch display, Ethernet port
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
After the Waveshare ESP32-S31-Touch-LCD-4.3C and VIEWE PLCM-UES31S043H800V480C-U, the GUITION JC1060F570C is another ESP32-S31 development kit with an integrated 7-inch touchscreen display. Some companies might reconsider the way they name their product… Leaving that aside, the GUITION devkit is especially interesting as it features a large 7-inch capacitive display compared to the 4.3-inch panels used in the other two models, and it’s the first to make use of the native Ethernet interface from the ESP32-S31 SoC. item.title: M5Stack Chain Captain – An ESP32-S3 multifunctional controller with 1.54-inch color display, audio, motion sensing, IR Tx/Rx
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
M5Stack Chain Captain is an ESP32-S3-based multifunctional programmable controller that features a 1.54-inch color square display, a speaker and microphone for audio interaction, motion sensing, and infrared transmission and reception. The IoT controller features 16MB SPI flash and 8MB on-chip PSRAM, Chain and Grove 4-pin ports, a 15-pin GPIO header, and several buttons and RGB. It’s powered by an 800 mAh battery that can be charged at 5V through USB-C or any of the expansion connectors. item.title: Raspberry Pi SBCs get an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module (Crowdfunding)
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
ANAVI I2C TPM 2.0 is an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module for Raspberry Pi single board computers based on the Infineon Optiga SLB 9673 TPM 2.0 chip. It’s an alternative to the earlier ANAVI TPM 2.0 module using an Optiga SLB 9672 SPI chip. The add-on board is designed for developers, hobbyists, and professionals who require enhanced security for Raspberry Pi-based projects. It’s especially useful for disk encryption, secure key storage, and cryptographic operations, but can also work as a True Hardware Random Number Generator (TRNG) for security-critical applications. item.title: Bluetooth 7.0 specification ratified with HDT (High Data Throughput) support
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
The Bluetooth SIG ratified the Bluetooth 7.0 specification on November 3, 2026, with the highlight of the new Bluetooth Core specification being optional support for HDT (High Data Throughput), delivering up to 7.5 Mbps bitrate. We first covered HDT in 2025 when initial/early support was implemented into the Ceva-Waves Links200 multi-protocol platform IP, and followed last September with the Realtek RTL8773J Bluetooth 7-ready Cortex-M55/M33 microcontroller. The main news is that the specification for Bluetooth 7.0 and the associated HDT feature is officially ratified/adopted. Bluetooth 7.0 highlights: Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT) introduces a new Bluetooth LE physical layer that increases the maximum Bluetooth bit rate to 7.5 Mbps while improving wireless efficiency and robustness. The higher bitrate is enabled by a combination of higher-order modulation, convolutional forward error correction, synchronization enhancements, adaptive rate selection, and enhanced packet architectures. It will be especially useful for high-resolution and lossless audio streaming. Bluetooth [...]

item.title: Web-based breadboard simulator lets you build circuits, fix errors, and monitor designs with a built-in oscilloscope
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
Dev Kapadia’s de:volt is a breadboard simulator that runs in your browser. You can place parts and wires on a breadboard, and the circuit runs live the whole time as you build it. The project aims to be as close as a real breadboard would be. It reports errors and warnings, and you can monitor pins with its built-in oscilloscope and/or multimeter. For instance, an LED with no resistor burns out, a weak battery sags under load, a motor pulls current, and a 555 on the 4-channel scope shows its timing capacitor charging and discharging. de:volt highlights: Build circuits on a virtual breadboard using the 105 parts available from the interface: resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors, LEDs, 555 timers, 74-series and CD4000 logic, EEPROMs, motor drivers, sensors, and more. Four Arduino, BBC micro:bit, and RP2040 MCU boards are also available, and you can write and run MicroPython code from the web [...]

item.title: Flipper One – A Rockchip RK3576-powered portable Arm Linux computer and networking multi-tool (Crowdfunding)
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
Flipper Devices has launched the Flipper One open-source hardware portable Arm Linux platform and networking/Edge AI multi-tool powered by a Rockchip RK3576 octa-core Arm Cortex-A72/A53 SoC. It also features a Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontroller for low-level control. You may think of it as a successor to the popular STM32-based Flipper Zero hardware and wireless hacking tool, but the company stresses that the Flipper One is NOT a replacement for the Flipper Zero. It is a different product with mainline Linux kernel support, no binary blobs (probably not 100% true), and open-source drivers, and operating at a different level of the networking and wireless stacks with dual Gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E, and optional 5G or 4G LTE modem. item.title: 750 MHz GigaDevice GD32H7 Cortex-M7 MCU family gets up to 9.5MB Flash, EtherCAT for industrial applications
item.dc:creator: Debashis Das
item.description:
GigaDevice adds new industrial parts to the GD32H7 series of Cortex-M7 MCUs, running at up to 750 MHz. The new lineup includes the GD32H77R for robotic joint control, GD32H78D/77D for industrial HMI applications, GD32H78E/77E for real-time motion control, and GD32H789/779 for general industrial automation. The MCUs feature up to 9728KB of on-chip Flash, 1152KB SRAM including 640KB tightly coupled memory (TCM), and hardware accelerators for mathematical operations and digital signal processing. Depending on the variant, they also integrate a MIPI DSI display interface, an EtherCAT slave controller, industrial encoder interfaces, dual Ethernet, and three CAN-FD controllers. The devices target servo drives, humanoid robots, industrial displays, CNC machines, PLCs, and digital power systems. GigaDevice GD32H7 new-generation industrial MCU specifications: MCU Core – 32-bit ARM Cortex-M7 core Up to 750 MHz (GD32H78D, GD32H78E, GD32H789 only) Up to 600 MHz (GD32H77R, GD32H77D, GD32H77E, GD32H779 only) Up to 3,736 CoreMark GPU – Image Processing Accelerator [...]

item.title: Rockchip RK3668 switches to Cortex-A725 and Cortex-A520 cores, engineering samples planned for Q1 2027
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
More details have surfaced about the Rockchip RK3668 processor. The biggest change is that the Armv9 SoC will feature eight cores (6x Cortex-A725 and 2x Cortex-A520), rather than ten cores in a 4x Cortex-A730 + 6x Cortex-A530 configuration announced at its initial unveiling in July 2025. Mostly because the A730 and A530 cores have never been launched… We also have more detailed specifications thanks to posts from Radxa and ArmSoM, who shared the “RK3668 Application” document. That document also includes a roadmap showing that the 6nm Rockchip RK3668 processor is now scheduled for Q1 2027 (engineering samples), and the flagship RK3688 processor should probably be available at the end of 2027 or in 2028, although the time scale in the roadmap may be deceiving… Early prototypes of RK3668 single board computers should come in H1 2027.   Rockchip RK3668 specifications: Octa-core CPU – 6x Cortex-A725 cores @ up to 2.5 [...]

item.title: $69 Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 controller offers PoE, audio streaming, RS-232 control, Bluetooth proxy, and more
item.dc:creator: Debashis Das
item.description:
Nabu Casa has launched the Home Assistant Connect AUX-2, an ESP32-S3-based smart home controller that combines audio streaming, RS-232 serial control, Bluetooth LE proxy, and USB expansion for Z-Wave connectivity. It is designed for older audio systems, TVs, AV receivers, UPSs, solar inverters, and other devices to integrate into Home Assistant without cloud services. More specifically, the device features a Texas Instruments PCM5122 DAC for analog and optical audio output, two RS-232 ports, a USB-A port, and a Grove connector for additional sensors. It also supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Ethernet with 802.3af Power over Ethernet (PoE), so you can install it away from the main Home Assistant server. item.title: Tektronix 1 Series low-cost DPO oscilloscopes support AI-assisted control, start at just $450

Tektronix is better known for its high-end and pricey oscilloscopes, but has now introduced the 1 Series DPO, a line of low-cost digital phosphor oscilloscopes starting at just $450, with optional AI-assisted control through the new Tek Intelligence connector. These oscilloscopes are designed for electronics testing, embedded development, education, and everyday circuit debugging. The 1 Series DPOs feature up to four analog channels, 50 MHz to 200 MHz bandwidth, 12-bit vertical resolution, and up to 1.25 GS/s sampling rate. They also integrate a 7-inch touchscreen and 10 Mpoints of memory per channel, support I2C, SPI, and UART protocol decoding, and implement built-in waveform analysis tools. The higher-priced S models add a 25 MHz arbitrary function generator (AFG) and Bode plot analysis. item.title: Home Assistant-compatible ESP32 4-channel PWM fan controller is designed for server racks and NAS systems
item.dc:creator: Debashis Das
item.description:
Designed by CoolMaker Lab in China, the ESP32 4-channel PWM fan controller is an open-source, Home Assistant-compatible board for managing cooling in server racks, NAS systems, network cabinets, and other DIY enclosures. It can independently control up to four 4-pin PWM fans, supporting PWM-based speed adjustment, tachometer-based RPM monitoring, and individual fan power switching. The controller supports up to four external DS18B20 temperature sensors for automatic fan speed adjustment, along with a web interface, an HTTP REST API, and Bluetooth proxy functionality. The latest v2.0 hardware and firmware also support optional LD2402G 24GHz mmWave radar for presence-based automation. item.title: Lumissil IS31CS9202/IS32CS9202 Cortex-M0+ MCUs integrate serial video bus (SBV), LumiBus, and capacitive touch-key controller
item.dc:creator: Jean-Luc Aufranc (CNXSoft)
item.description:
Lumissil Microsystems IS31CS9202 and IS32CS9202 are 50 MHz Cortex-M0+ microcontrollers for industrial, consumer, and automotive applications with a serial video bus (SVB), a LumiBus LED controller, and a capacitive touch-key controller. Both chips come with 16KB RAM, 256KB flash, a CAN FD controller, SPI master/slave, I2C master/slave, two enhanced UART interfaces, a quadrature encoder, a 14-bit sigma-delta ADC, a 12-bit SAR ADC, an 8-bit DAC, up to 42 GPIO pins, and more. item.title: Renesas RZ/T2N Cortex-A55/R52 industrial MPU supports four-axis motor control, TSN Ethernet, EtherCAT…
item.dc:creator: Debashis Das
item.description:
Renesas RZ/T2N industrial MPU supports up to four-axis motor control and includes PWM timers, encoder interfaces, and trigonometric accelerators. It’s designed for industrial robots, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), motion controllers, and multi-axis servo drives. The MPU features up to two 1.2 GHz Arm Cortex-A55 cores for application processing and two 800 MHz Cortex-R52 cores for real-time control. It also integrates a three-port Gigabit Ethernet switch with TSN support and industrial Ethernet protocols such as EtherCAT, PROFINET RT/IRT, and EtherNet/IP. This feature set allows real-time motor control, industrial networking, and Linux applications to run on a single chip, reducing the need for separate processors. The MPU can also work as an industrial Ethernet network controller or device, depending on the application. item.title: LocalDot – Open-source PCB for 3rd-gen Amazon Echo Dot enables Home Assistant support (Crowdfunding)
item.dc:creator: Debashis Das
item.description:
AAElectronics’ LocalDot is an open-source replacement mainboard that converts a 3rd-generation Amazon Echo Dot into a local voice assistant compatible with Home Assistant. The board replaces one of the two original PCBs while reusing the existing microphones, speaker, buttons, LEDs, and enclosure, so the device works without relying on Amazon’s cloud services. The board combines an ESP32-S3 for WiFi connectivity and device control with an ESP32-P4 for audio processing. It supports the original four-microphone array with beamforming, on-device wake-word detection, and local voice commands through Home Assistant. Installation requires no soldering or enclosure modifications, and the device still uses the original Echo Dot power adapter.
